Grounds & Landscaping Crew

LIUNA, SEIU and AFSCME grounds and landscaping crews

LIUNA, SEIU and AFSCME grounds and landscaping crew training, tested against OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general industry standards, ANSI B71 and B175 outdoor power equipment and chainsaw specifications, ANSI Z133 arboricultural safety, the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) pesticide label, the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) and CPSC movable soccer goal guidance across twelve distinct grounds, turf and landscaping jobs

Twelve jobs a grounds crew actually rotates through: a ride-on mower's own pre-start and slope work, a string trimmer and blower run inside a posted bystander zone, an irrigation controller and backflow assembly serviced and tested, a labelled pesticide mixed and applied per the label, a pole saw's drop zone controlled under a spotter's signal, a chainsaw started and limbed on the ground with the chain brake proven first, a bunker rebuilt around a graded drain line, a green mowed and its hole changed, a sports field striped and its goals anchored to the manufacturer's own spec, a storm-damaged shoulder cleared with a chipper behind a traffic taper, a paver patio built on a compacted, checked base, and a nursery's chemical storage kept segregated with its eyewash actually flow-tested. Every station ends on a proof — a gauge, a logged reading, a checked interlock — rather than on how safe the job looked going in.

The ladder

Grounds & Landscaping

Ride-On Mower Pre-Start & Slope Work

16 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

The walk-around and the interlocks are confirmed before the seat is ever sat in, the bench is walked for the drop-off and the wet patch a wheel cannot see coming, and the slope is cut the way the machine's own operator's manual sets out.

  • ANSI — ANSI B71 series — safety specifications for outdoor power equipment (walk-behind and riding mowers, trimmers and blowers), published with the Outdoor Power Equipment Institute
  • union — LIUNA Training and Education Fund — construction craft laborer, hazardous waste and environmental remediation curricula
  • NIOSH — NIOSH criteria documents, Health Hazard Evaluations and the Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.132 — Personal protective equipment, general requirements
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.147 — The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.212 — General requirements for all machines (machine guarding)
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.95 — Occupational noise exposure

Trimmer & Blower PPE and Bystander Zone

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.8 min

Irrigation Controller, Valve Box & Backflow Check

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

What it proves

Competency: Run, service and make safe the mowers, chemicals, saws and turf equipment a grounds crew works across twelve distinct jobs

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 6 of its 12 stations, against ANSI ANSI B71 series — safety specifications for outdoor power equipment (walk-behind and riding mowers, trimmers and blowers), published with the Outdoor Power Equipment Institute; ANSI ANSI Z133 — safety requirements for arboricultural operations, including chippers used on a tree crew; EPA Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) — the pesticide product label as a legal document, and EPA's pesticide applicator and worker-protection requirements; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout).

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: LIUNA, SEIU and AFSCME grounds and landscaping crew training, tested against OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general industry standards, ANSI B71 and B175 outdoor power equipment and chainsaw specifications, ANSI Z133 arboricultural safety, the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) pesticide label, the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) and CPSC movable soccer goal guidance across twelve distinct grounds, turf and landscaping jobs. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
